Come out and become visible — Emerger / salir.
The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
Become known — Salir a la luz.
New facts emerged during the trial.
With rough sharp points — Dentado/a / irregular.
He cut his hand on the jagged glass.
Stay longer than expected — Quedarse / demorarse.
We lingered at the table after dinner.
A surprise attack from a hiding place — Emboscada.
The convoy was caught in an ambush.
Attack from hiding — Emboscar / tender una emboscada a.
Clever at tricking people — Astuto/a / taimado/a.
A crafty salesman sold him the car.
Openly refusing to obey — Desafiante / rebelde.
The boy gave a defiant answer.
He attacked the job with vigor.
Die, especially in a terrible way — Perecer / morir.
Be destroyed or rot — Echarse a perder / deteriorarse.
v|Formal. In everyday speech people say die.
Weak and easily damaged — Delicado/a / endeble.
Kept as a prisoner — Cautivo/a / en cautiverio.
Do well and become successful — Prosperar.
The business prospered after the move.
She devours three books a week.
He made a plea for help.
A prisoner's answer in court — Declaración / alegato.
She entered a plea of not guilty.
Verb: plead. Pattern: a plea for something.
After the climb we were weary.
I am weary of his excuses.
Hit something while moving — Chocar / colisionar.
The two cars collided at the corner.
Be in strong disagreement — Chocar / enfrentarse.
v|Noun: collision. Pattern: collide with something.
Show that something is true — Confirmar.
Say definitely that something will happen — Confirmar.
Check that something is true — Verificar / comprobar.
Expect something to happen — Prever / anticipar.
Look forward to — Esperar con ilusión.
She anticipated the trip for months.
A hard choice between two bad options — Dilema.
Phrase: to be in a dilemma.
A longer way round — Desvío / rodeo.
We took a detour to avoid the traffic.
Go the long way round — Desviarse / dar un rodeo.
The bus detoured through the village.
Send a signal or message — Transmitir.
The station transmits in two languages.
Make pain or worry less — Aliviar.
The night nurse relieved her at ten.
Admit that something is true — Reconocer / admitir.
Say you have received something — Acusar recibo de.
Fair treatment under the law — Justicia.
A judge, in some courts — Juez / magistrado.
Person who breaks the law, often young — Delincuente.
Late in paying — En mora / moroso/a.
Something thrown out as not good enough — Desecho / pieza defectuosa.
v|Noun: rejection. The verb is stressed last, the noun first.
Take something away from someone — Privar de.
The illness deprived him of his sight.
v|Pattern: deprive someone of something. Noun: deprivation.
Bring your spouse to the dinner.
The work a person feels called to do — Vocación.
A job or profession — Oficio / profesión.
He chose nursing as his vocation.
Adjective: vocational, as in vocational training.
Not firm; likely to fall or change — Inestable.
The killing of one person by another — Homicidio.
The police treated it as a homicide.
Legal word. Everyday English says murder or killing.
Punish; give a penalty to — Penalizar / sancionar.
Put someone at a disadvantage — Perjudicar.
Person who receives money or benefit — Beneficiario/a.
She is the beneficiary of the insurance.
Cold-blooded animal such as a snake or lizard — Reptil.
Not often — Rara vez / pocas veces.
Goes before the main verb: I rarely go. Adjective: rare.
Order someone not to do something — Prohibir.
Her parents forbid her to go out alone.
v|Pattern: forbid someone to do something, or forbid doing something.
That is the logical next step.
Show something in public — Exponer / exhibir.
Something put on show — Muestra / pieza expuesta.
v|Noun: exhibition. The h is silent: eg-ZIB-it.
Go on after stopping — Proceder / continuar.
After the break we proceeded with the meeting.
v|Noun: procedure. Careful: proceed is to go on, precede is to go before.
Something done in advance to avoid trouble — Precaución / medida preventiva.
Take an umbrella as a precaution.
Pull something out with effort — Extraer / sacar.
A short piece taken from a text — Extracto / fragmento.
Read this extract from the book.
v|The verb is stressed last, the noun first.
Coming before in time — Previo/a / anterior.
I had no prior knowledge of the plan.
Phrase: prior to, meaning before. Noun: priority.
He made a valiant attempt to save them.
Unfairly favouring one side — Parcial / sesgado/a.
I am partial to dark chocolate.
Adverb: partially. Opposite of the second sense: impartial.
